confidence_notes: I used web searches to set the food and drink anchors. Two Numbeo listings for Seattle (Nov 2026) and Wise listings (2026) gave an inexpensive meal at about $21-25, a mid-range meal for two without drinks at about $100, a cappuccino at about $6.10-6.65 and a domestic 0.5L draft beer at about $8. Expatica and Expatistan gave similar figures, but one Expatistan snapshot may be older than its label. Most cocktail estimates from travel and price guides fell between $16 and $22, with averages around $16-18. I found no reliable average for a glass of wine. The wine figure is my own judgment, based on a few undated menu examples at about $15-16 and the usual local price gap over beer, so it is the least certain drink anchor. All four accommodation anchors are general-knowledge estimates for Seattle's July peak season. I did not search for them or check any live listings. Seattle has only a few registered hostels, so the dorm and private hostel figures could vary by about 25%. July hotel prices change a lot with cruise and event demand.
comparable_city_reasoning: Based mainly on aggregated Seattle price data. I checked accommodation against general knowledge of other expensive US West Coast cities in peak summer: Seattle sits below San Francisco and above Portland.
